title: Finite product descent through rationalization and common coefficient fields
statement:
Fix the global field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$, $i\in I$, be a finite pairwise disjoint open and closed cover [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

For every finite coefficient field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, use its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, and put $\mathcal C_E(Y)=D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Assume the component restrictions are $\mathcal O_E$-linear equivalences $\mathcal C_E(X)\simeq\prod_i\mathcal C_E(X_i)$ and that their natural comparisons preserve completed tensor, coefficient units, and integral scalar extension for every inclusion $E\subset L$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-weil-integral-scalar-extension].

The rationalized restrictions induce equivalences
$$D^b_c(X,E)\simeq\prod_iD^b_c(X_i,E)$$
for the raw scalar localizations of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. On Hom groups these use the canonical isomorphism
$$\left(\prod_i H_i\right)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_i\left(H_i\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\right),\qquad (h_i)_i\otimes a\longmapsto(h_i\otimes a)_i,$$
where $H_i$ are the integral component Hom modules. They commute with the coefficient extensions $E\subset L$ and preserve the rational tensor and unit of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

The common-stage restriction functor for [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] is also an equivalence
$$D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)\simeq\prod_iD^b_c(X_i,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell).$$
Every finite tuple of component objects has a preimage represented over one finite coefficient field containing their fields of definition. Every finite tuple of component morphisms has a simultaneous representative and a global preimage over one common finite extension. Two global arrows have equal component classes if and only if their representatives agree globally after some common finite extension. These comparisons respect identities, composition, tensor products and coefficient units, using the canonical finite-stage scalar-extension comparisons. At field stages $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], so these equivalences also apply to the stated finite-Tor categories. No Karoubi completion is taken. The empty product is permitted.

proof.text: For each $E$, apply [lem-pur-raw-localization-finite-product-equivalence] to $R=\mathcal O_E$, $t=\varpi_E$ and the assumed integral restriction equivalence. By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] its scalar localization has $S=E$ and is exactly the stated raw rational category. This gives $R_E$, the equivalence and its specified Hom tensor formula, including the empty product.

source.place: Final invertibility assertion, finite-clopen coefficient transport; assembly step 1 of the Q126 re-split.

proof.text: Each $X_i$ is a finite-type $k$-scheme: $j_i$ is a closed immersion, hence of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](a), and its composite with the finite-type structure morphism of $X$ is of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](1). Apply [lem-pur-rational-restriction-comparison-coherence] to each $j_i:X_i\to X$. Its integral mixed squares are precisely the assumed preservation of integral scalar extension by the restriction tensor and unit comparisons. Thus the canonical rational $b,\theta,\mu,\epsilon$ are natural, with the identity/tower and mixed squares required below.

source.place: Final invertibility assertion, finite-clopen coefficient transport; assembly step 2 of the Q126 re-split.

proof.text: Step 1 gives rational essential surjectivity, and step 2 gives the canonical coherent $b$. Therefore [lem-pur-common-stage-finite-object-lifting] supplies the common-stage restriction functor and simultaneous object preimages over one finite field, with the prescribed component isomorphisms.

source.place: Final invertibility assertion, finite-clopen coefficient transport; assembly step 3 of the Q126 re-split.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-common-stage-finite-hom-lifting] using rational full faithfulness from step 1 and the same $b$. It gives simultaneous arrow lifts, Hom bijections and the iff for eventual global equality. For arrows between arbitrary component tuples, conjugate by the object isomorphisms of step 3 and apply this bijection. The finitely many fields of those arrows and isomorphisms can be included in the common field.

source.place: Final invertibility assertion, finite-clopen coefficient transport; assembly step 4 of the Q126 re-split.

proof.text: Steps 3-4 satisfy [lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence] in a common enlarged universe, proving the algebraically closed coefficient equivalence. Apply [lem-pur-common-stage-restriction-tensor-descent] componentwise to the comparisons of step 2: it gives the common-stage tensor and unit comparisons, representative independence and their structural equations. Its scalar-unit identifications are the canonical finite-stage coefficient-unit identifications in the statement. Identities and composition are already part of step 3.

source.place: Final invertibility assertion, finite-clopen coefficient transport; assembly step 5 of the Q126 re-split.

proof.text: The three finite-product lifting results explicitly allow $I=\varnothing$; their empty-field choice is $\mathbf Q_\ell$, enlarged only for specified endpoints or representatives, and the Hom sets are singletons. Finally [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] defines both field-stage finite-Tor categories to equal $D^b_c$. All categories and comparisons above use unchanged integral objects and finite-stage pairs, so none takes a Karoubi completion.
